name: Desktop Agent
author: Zedster07
description: Voice control and agent control for your desktop, on a leash you own. Push-to-talk dictation that types into any window, spoken commands matched against a declared registry, and a default-deny policy with an approval overlay and an audit trail.

barWidget.description: Voice dictation, spoken commands, and policy-gated agent control with an approval overlay and kill switch.

schema.label: Voice input
schema.description: Enable push-to-talk dictation and spoken commands. Turning this off unloads the voice daemon entirely.

schema.label: Speech engine
schema.description: whisper.cpp is the widest language coverage. moonshine is fastest for short push-to-talk phrases. parakeet is the most accurate in English. Only engines detected on this machine are offered at runtime.

schema.label: Model size
schema.description: Larger is more accurate and much slower, and latency matters more than accuracy for dictation. base is ~1.2s on an 8-thread 2016 CPU; small was ~4.6s on the same machine. Run `desktop-agent benchmark` to measure yours before moving up.

schema.label: Language code
schema.description: Forced, never auto-detected. Auto-detection on short audio is a common cause of a phrase coming back translated instead of transcribed.

schema.label: Text injection
schema.description: wtype types directly via the Wayland virtual-keyboard protocol. clipboard-paste is the fallback for apps that ignore synthetic key events; it restores your previous clipboard afterwards.

schema.label: Preview before inserting
schema.description: Show the transcript in the voice HUD and wait for Enter instead of typing it straight away. Off is faster; on is safer when dictating into something consequential.

schema.label: Custom vocabulary
schema.description: Comma-separated names, jargon, and project terms used to prime the decoder. Markedly improves accuracy on technical words the model would otherwise guess at.

schema.label: Spoken commands
schema.description: Enable command mode, where a spoken phrase is matched against the intent registry and run through the policy instead of being typed as text.

schema.label: Confirm spoken commands
schema.description: Whether a matched command shows a confirmation in the HUD before it runs. This is layered on top of the policy, which can still force an approval regardless.

schema.label: Let other plugins register commands
schema.description: Read voice-intents.json from other installed Omarchy plugins so their actions can be spoken. Each newly discovered plugin has to be approved once before its intents become live.

schema.label: Agent control (MCP)
schema.description: Allow an MCP client such as Claude Code to drive the desktop through the same policy. Voice works with this off.

schema.label: End-of-run recap
schema.description: After the agent has been idle a while, slide in a card listing everything it did. Never takes focus.

schema.label: Recap idle window (seconds)
schema.description: MCP has no end-of-task signal, so a run counts as finished once the desktop has been quiet this long.

schema.label: Maximum unattended lease (minutes)
schema.description: Hard ceiling on a full-access lease, re-checked on every action. A longer lease is truncated, not honoured.

schema.label: Model folder
schema.description: Where speech models are stored. Leave empty for ~/.local/share/desktop-agent/models.
